name: Party Games
oneLine: Ain't It Awful, Blemish, Schlemiel, and Why Don't You...?-Yes, But... are the games that structure casual social time, usually at first degree.
whatYouDid: You classified Karan's running commentary on everyone's flaws as Blemish, a Party game, rather than a Consulting-Room, Underworld, or Good game, and - in the boss round - hunted down the exact antithesis to Why Don't You...?/Yes, But...
confusion: Why Don't You...? reads as a genuine offer of help, and Yes, But... reads as a genuine request for it; the tell that it's a Party game instead is that the content of every suggestion is nearly irrelevant - the same shape runs whether it's suggestion three or suggestion thirty.

fromBook.quote: In Blemish, the player finds fault with others, criticizing their appearance, work, dress, etc.

expand.definition: Party games are first-degree, social-time-structuring games - Blemish picks at others' faults, Why Don't You...? supplies an endless stream of suggestions, and Yes, But... rejects every one of them without ever quite saying "I don't want advice."
expand.otherFraming: Most named games collapse into a small number of basic Drama-Triangle-switch patterns; Why Don't You...? and Yes, But... are the two halves of a single Rescuer-to-Victim / Victim-to-Persecutor pairing, played from opposite chairs.
expand.tryThisToday: At your next group hangout, count how many "why don't you" suggestions get a "yes, but" in response - if it's more than one or two, you're watching the Response stage of a live game.
